title: Tenant isolation routing shards and hosted backfill protections
creator: Amelia Park
description: Problem: During high utilization windows some tenants on Dedicated pools experienced degraded latency when hosted spillover kicked in; the current spillover routing is too coarse-grained and can cause noisy neighbors to backfill capacity in ways that violate tenant SLAs or inflate cost unexpectedly. We need a routing/sharding policy that preserves tenant isolation guarantees for Dedicated customers while still allowing safe hosted backfill when capacity is exhausted.
background: Existing work (see ENG-41289 and ENG-21473) adds region-tier steering and priority decay throttles, but does not provide per-tenant shard affinity nor cost-protecting backfill rules. Incidents in 2025-04 (pager on 2025-04-17) showed two mid-market customers on the same Dedicated shard saw 3x latency variance when hosted spillover returned partial capacity for certain tenants. Investigations point to: lack of tenant-shard affinity, no preemptive throttles for hosted backfill, and insufficient variant-weighting logic when switching to cheaper hosted model variants.
goals: 1) Implement tenant-shard affinity to avoid cross-tenant interference within a Dedicated shard. 2) Add hosted-backfill protections: rate-limited backfill, per-tenant budget caps, and SLA-first routing so critical tenants are not sent to lower-quality hosted variants. 3) Expose config knobs in Console for tenant owners to opt into aggressive backfill or strict isolation. 4) Provide observability: per-tenant backfill metrics, cost delta estimates, and an automated rollback trigger when latency/SLO regressions are detected.
success_metrics:
- <10% increase in p95 latency for priority tenants during peak hosted-backfill events (measured over 7-day windows)
- Reduction of cross-tenant latency covariance by 50% on Dedicated shards
- No unexpected billing spikes >20% caused by automatic hosted backfill for dedicated customers (monitored per-tenant)
- Console feature adoption: 25% of eligible tenants configure isolation/backfill preferences within first month
acceptance_criteria:
- Routing engine supports tenant->shard affinity keys and respects affinity during placements and rebalances.
- Hosted backfill flow implements: (a) token-rate limiter per-tenant, (b) per-tenant monthly cost cap with hard/soft modes, (c) SLA-first flag that prevents sending to lower-quality hosted variants unless manual override.
- Console UI surfaces isolation/backfill toggles and expected cost/latency tradeoffs.
- End-to-end tests covering failover to hosted variant, quota exhaustion, and automatic rollback trigger based on latency regression thresholds.
- Monitoring dashboards with per-tenant backfill usage and alerting rules added to PagerDuty playbooks.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
1) Sharding granularity: we prefer tenant-level affinity to application-level multi-tenant shards to minimize blast radius, but this increases scheduling pressure and may reduce packing efficiency (tradeoff: isolation vs utilization).
2) Hosted backfill throttling: soft vs hard caps. Soft caps give flexibility but risk cost surprises; default will be soft with Console opt-in for hard cap.
3) Variant fallbacks: prefer capacity-compatible variants in same performance class. We will avoid automatic fallback to aggressively quantized variants for tenants with SLA-first set — requires tagging model variants with quality_class metadata.
4) Preemptive draining: when a Dedicated shard becomes overloaded, we will prefer tenant-specific throttling and queued requests rather than mass failover to hosted endpoints to prioritize latency SLOs for high-tier customers.
implementation_plan:
1) Routing layer: extend placement engine to store tenant affinity keys; enforce during shuffle/reassign. (ENG owners: Diego, Naz)
2) Backfill controller: implement per-tenant token bucket and monthly cost accounting; integrate with billing service for cost caps. (Owners: Priya, Omar)
3) Variant tagging: add quality_class metadata to model catalog and extend smart-routing policy to consult quality_class and tenant SLA. (Owners: Rohan, Mei)
4) Console: add Backfill Preferences panel (toggle: strict isolation / balanced / aggressive backfill) and cost preview. (Owners: Lina, Marco)
5) E2E tests and canary release: staged rollout to internal beta tenants then select paying Dedicated tenants.
6) Observability: dashboards, alerting, and automated rollback runbook (owners: SRE, Observability team).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for affinity matching and token-bucket behavior.
- Integration test harness simulating multi-tenant load with controlled skew to verify isolation and backfill behavior.
- Chaos test: randomly kill Dedicated workers during a scenario to validate correct and safe hosted spillover with cost/latency guards.
- Performance benchmark: measure scheduling latency impact of tenant affinity at 10k tenant simulations.
- Beta with 5 Dedicated customers under traffic patterns representing spike, flash-drop, and sustained high utilization.
monitoring_and_runbook:
- Dashboards: per-tenant p50/p95 latency, percent requests served on Dedicated vs Hosted, backfill cost delta, token-bucket depletion events.
- Alerts: (1) tenant_p95 increase >20% over baseline for 5m -> paging; (2) hosted_backfill_cost > 20% of tenant budget in 24h -> notify on-call and customer success; (3) more than 10% of requests spilled to hosted for a single shard in 10m -> warn.
- Runbook short flow: detect -> throttle hosts -> engage preemptive queue -> rollback if SLA > threshold -> postmortem. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/routing/backfill-runbook (internal).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy routing + backfill controller to canary region for internal tenants (2 weeks). Phase 2 (beta): opt-in for 5 paying Dedicated tenants with close monitoring (4 weeks). Phase 3 (gradual): enable default soft backfill globally for low-tier tenants and keep strict isolation as default for Dedicated with SLA. Provide migration notes for tenants on older shard assignments.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Increased fragmentation of Dedicated capacity leading to wasted GPUs. Mitigation: periodic compaction job that consolidates low-traffic tenants during off-peak windows.
Risk: Cost surprises to tenants when soft caps are exceeded. Mitigation: default to soft caps with explicit Console warnings and email notifications; provide hard cap opt-in.
Risk: Scheduling latency regression when enforcing affinity at scale. Mitigation: benchmark + optimize placement (approximate affinity heuristics) and fall back to relaxed affinity under cluster pressure.
